pairs.subject: companion-runtime
pairs.evidence: app/api/companion/[id]/message/route.ts:76 The HTTP route itself chooses the prompt window, writes the user turn, derives the title and persists the reply, so turn logic lives in the transport; there is also no server-side lock per conversation (only the dock coalesces on the client), so two tabs can run concurrent turns on one thread.

techniques.evidence: app/api/companion/[id]/message/route.ts:76 The adapter assembles history, writes turns (lines 83, 121) and renames the thread (89). runCompanionTurn returns a single result, not an event stream. No lock keyed on conversation identity; concurrency is only coalesced client-side (comment at line 44). The digest task (companion-digest-run.ts:62) re-implements the same reply persistence, which is the hand-parity shape the standard names.

app/api/companion/proposals/[id]/resolve/route.ts:106 At acceptance the proposal is re-checked against the catalog (companionAction + coerceCompanionAction at line 115). A kind the catalog has dropped is retired with a 'retired' outcome instead of being run. The atomic claim/release keeps the mutation approval-gated.
